title: Suspected bacterial meningitis at 45 on long-term prednisone, ampicillin already ordered

provenance.author: Claude Code (draft for owner review), Listeria risk-factor rule (owner decision 2026-11-12)

story: A 45-year-old woman with pulmonary sarcoidosis on prednisone 20 mg a day for six months presents with fever, severe headache, neck stiffness and new confusion. Lumbar puncture shows a neutrophilic pleocytosis with low glucose and high protein. Empiric vancomycin, ceftriaxone 2 g every 12 hours, ampicillin 2 g every 4 hours and dexamethasone are started; CSF and blood cultures are pending.

problems.title: Long term (current) use of systemic steroids

reference_answer: No intervention: the empiric regimen covers Listeria, which long-term corticosteroids make more likely. Some reviews prefer cefepime or meropenem in immunocompromised hosts; the rules do not flag ceftriaxone. Narrow therapy when cultures return.
rationale: Long-term systemic steroids are a Listeria risk factor (ESCMID 2016: immunosuppressive drugs; WHO 2025: immunosuppressive therapy), and ampicillin is already ordered, so the rule must stay silent. No meningitis guideline sets a steroid dose threshold; the rule reads the long-term steroid problem code.

citations.supports: Empiric amoxicillin or ampicillin for Listeria, added to cefotaxime or ceftriaxone, in adults over 50 and in adults 18 to 50 with Listeria risk factors (Table 4.1 footnote: diabetes mellitus, immunosuppressive drugs, cancer, other immunocompromising conditions).
Add ampicillin or amoxicillin to the initial empiric regimen with any Listeria risk factor, including immunosuppressive therapy; checked against the WHO document, 2026-11-12.
